desc:
You are given a lowercase string s and a list of shifts. Each shift is a triple [left, right, direction]. It moves every letter in positions left..right (inclusive) one step through the alphabet: forward if direction = 1 (a becomes b, ..., z becomes a), backward if direction = 0 (b becomes a, ..., a becomes z).

Apply all the shifts and return the final string.

s = "xyz", shifts = [[0, 1, 1], [1, 2, 1], [0, 2, 0]]
result = "xzz"

The string goes xyz → yzz → yaa → xzz.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Shifting letter by letter for each operation is O(n) per shift. Think about what the final letter at one position depends on.
Each position ends up shifted by (number of forward shifts covering it) minus (number of backward shifts covering it), taken modulo 26. The order of shifts does not matter.
Use a difference array: +1 for a forward shift and -1 for a backward one at left, the opposite at right + 1. A prefix sum gives the net shift per position; apply it modulo 26.
editorial: Every shift is a +1 or -1 on a range of positions, and shifts commute, so only the net shift of each position matters. Position i gets net cover_forward(i) - cover_backward(i), applied to its letter modulo 26.

A difference array records the net effect of all shifts in O(1) each; a single prefix sum recovers the net shift of every position. Be careful with negative sums: reduce with a proper modulo (in Python % already returns a non-negative value). Time O(n + m), space O(n).
